what_this_is: The after-figure for phase 38. Read against baseline/38-BASELINE-realtime.pre-38.json, which was captured before this migration existed on disk. A number with no before is not evidence of a change, so every probe here names its pre-38 counterpart.
probe_method: POST /v1/projects/{ref}/database/query with read_only: true (runs as supabase_read_only_user) for every probe, plus GET /v1/projects/{ref}/config/realtime. The single write was the migrations-endpoint apply recorded under `apply`. Nothing else wrote to production.

apply.why_not_database_query: /database/query applies DDL while writing nothing into the project migration history. Using it here would have added a nineteenth gap to the eighteen that already predate this phase. Precedent: phase 36 applied 20260810144239 through the migrations endpoint, phase 37 applied 20260810210214.
apply.note_on_the_assigned_version: The endpoint assigns its own wall-clock version (20260811111530) and does not adopt the filename's timestamp (20260811120000). Same behaviour as phases 36 and 37, and the reason the version is recorded here rather than inferred from the filename.

preflight.why: The four triggers land on the check-in write path and a DDL transaction takes locks on those tables for the moment it runs. T-38-04-06 accepts that risk only outside a night, so it was measured rather than assumed. Counts only — no name, no date, no venue: this repository is public.

cascade_enumeration.method: Every foreign key in the database was read from pg_constraint (contype = 'f') — 102 edges — and the graph was walked in BOTH directions from the four trigger tables until closure. Not remembered, not eyeballed: phase 37 found the true count was 18 and not 17 because discount_code_tiers arrives at two hops through two different paths.
cascade_enumeration.gated_set_composition: The public-schema closure (25 tables) plus the two private-schema tables the closure reaches. The migration creates into `private`, so those belong under the gate.
cascade_enumeration.why_auth_is_observed_and_not_gated: The 13 auth-schema tables are in the full closure (public.profiles references auth.users) but the auth service writes auth.sessions, auth.refresh_tokens and auth.one_time_tokens on any login or token refresh, independently of this transaction. Gating on them would manufacture a false failure that hides the signal the gate exists to carry. They are counted on both sides anyway and reported — and they did not move either.
cascade_enumeration.d12: All seven tables of the 2026-08-10 incident (D12 — 63 rows lost, no PITR) are inside the gated set: drink_orders, drink_tokens, drink_items, pending_purchases, tickets, ticket_tiers, guest_list_entries.

rowcounts_comparison: All 27 tables in the gated cascade set hold an identical count before and after the apply — 81 rows in total on both sides. Zero rows were written, updated or deleted. Demonstrated, not asserted.
rowcounts_observed_comparison: The 13 observed auth-schema tables also hold identical counts before and after.

realtime_policies.qual:
CASE
    WHEN (extension <> 'broadcast'::text) THEN false
    WHEN (( SELECT realtime.topic() AS topic) ~ '^door:[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$'::text) THEN ( SELECT private.has_capability('door.operate'::text, (SUBSTRING(( SELECT realtime.topic() AS topic) FROM 6))::uuid) AS has_capability)
    ELSE false
END

realtime_policies__query: select policyname, cmd, roles::text as roles, qual from pg_policies where schemaname = 'realtime'
realtime_policies__reading: Exactly one policy, cmd SELECT, TO authenticated, named realtime_messages_select_door_assigned. Its qual is read AS POSTGRES RENDERS IT, not as the file reads: the topic regex is evaluated in a CASE arm BEFORE the ::uuid cast, so a malformed topic is a false and not a 22P02 — and an error inside a policy is a refused connection, not a denied row. The predicate names private.has_capability and the literal 'door.operate' and nothing else: no second definition of "assigned to this night" was introduced. LIVE-06.
write_policies__query: select policyname, cmd, roles::text as roles, qual from pg_policies where schemaname = 'realtime' and cmd <> 'SELECT'
write_policies__pre38: [] — there were no policies at all
write_policies__reading: Zero. With relrowsecurity = true and anon/authenticated each already holding table-level arw on realtime.messages (38-01, messages_acl_expanded), the ABSENCE of any INSERT policy is what makes the database the only sender. The gap is the boundary, not unfinished work.
messages_relstate__pre38: relrowsecurity true, relforcerowsecurity false, owner supabase_realtime_admin

source_table_triggers__query: select tgname, tgrelid::regclass::text as tbl, pg_get_triggerdef(oid) as def from pg_trigger where not tgisinternal and tgrelid::regclass::text in ('door_scan_events','tickets','guest_list_entries','ticket_refunds') order by tbl, tgname
source_table_triggers__difference: Before: 0 triggers across the four tables. After: 4, one per table — door_scan_events (AFTER INSERT), tickets (AFTER INSERT OR DELETE OR UPDATE), guest_list_entries (AFTER INSERT OR DELETE OR UPDATE), ticket_refunds (AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE). The difference is +4, on four tables and not three.
helper_acl__query: select n.nspname, p.proname, p.prosecdef, p.proconfig::text as proconfig, p.proacl::text as proacl, p.proowner::regrole::text as proowner, pg_get_function_identity_arguments(p.oid) as args from pg_proc p join pg_namespace n on n.oid = p.pronamespace where p.proname = 'notify_attendance_changed'
helper_acl__reading: F1 CLOSED IN PRODUCTION. Exactly one notify_attendance_changed, in schema private, prosecdef true, search_path pinned to the empty string, owned by postgres. proacl is NON-NULL — {postgres=X/postgres} — which is the point: a null proacl would have meant the default EXECUTE to PUBLIC still applied and the REVOKE had not taken. It grants EXECUTE to the owner and to nobody else: no bare =X/ entry (PUBLIC), no anon, no authenticated.

direct_call_probe.what: Leg (a) of the event_media_party_id paragraph, and F1, measured rather than cited. Each call was made through /database/query with read_only: true, so the whole transaction was READ ONLY and no write could have landed whatever the answer was.
direct_call_probe.select public.tickets_notify_attendance(: 0A000: trigger functions can only be called as triggers
direct_call_probe.select public.door_scan_events_notify_at: 0A000: trigger functions can only be called as triggers
direct_call_probe.reading: The four wrappers carry a permissive proacl — {=X/postgres, anon=X/postgres, authenticated=X/postgres, …}, the Supabase default for a function created in public by postgres — and that grants nobody anything, because a RETURNS trigger function cannot be called directly at all. The helper, which IS an ordinary callable, refuses with 42501 from a role that is not its owner. That refusal is F1 closed behaviourally, which is worth more than reading an ACL and inferring it.

realtime_send_body__query: select p.prosrc from pg_proc p join pg_namespace n on n.oid = p.pronamespace where n.nspname = 'realtime' and p.proname = 'send'
realtime_send_body__pre38: measured 2026-08-11 (38-01): prosecdef false, and the insert wrapped in EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS THEN RAISE WARNING
realtime_send_body__reading: Unchanged after the apply: the insert is still wrapped in EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS THEN RAISE WARNING, so realtime.send cannot raise and the two triggers on the money tables cannot fail a purchase, a check-in or a refund. Re-asserting it after the change costs one query and is the difference between a citation and a check. The same property is the reason a failed emit is invisible outside the Postgres log — which is why the door keeps its 5-minute parachute.

wrapper_bodies.def:
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.ticket_refunds_notify_attendance()
 RETURNS trigger
 LANGUAGE plpgsql
 SECURITY DEFINER
 SET search_path TO ''
AS $function$
BEGIN
  PERFORM private.notify_attendance_changed(NEW.refunded_party_id, NEW.refunded_event_id);

  IF TG_OP = 'UPDATE'
     AND (OLD.refunded_party_id, OLD.refunded_event_id)
         IS DISTINCT FROM (NEW.refunded_party_id, NEW.refunded_event_id)
  THEN
    PERFORM private.notify_attendance_changed(OLD.refunded_party_id, OLD.refunded_event_id);
  END IF;

  RETURN NULL;
END;
$function$

wrapper_bodies__query: select p.proname, p.prosecdef, p.proconfig::text as proconfig, p.proacl::text as proacl, pg_get_functiondef(p.oid) as def from pg_proc p join pg_namespace n on n.oid = p.pronamespace where n.nspname = 'public' and p.proname in ('tickets_notify_attendance', 'guest_list_entries_notify_attendance', 'ticket_refunds_notify_attendance') order by p.proname
wrapper_bodies__reading: D-38-24 measured on what LANDED rather than on what was written. All three update-capable wrappers — tickets, guest_list_entries, ticket_refunds — contain IS DISTINCT FROM and two calls to private.notify_attendance_changed in their applied definitions. Without the old-pair emit, a row moved between two nights of an event tells only the destination door; the origin door — the one that just lost an attendee — falls back to the parachute with every screen still looking right.

door_wrapper.def:
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.door_scan_events_notify_attendance()
 RETURNS trigger
 LANGUAGE plpgsql
 SECURITY DEFINER
 SET search_path TO ''
AS $function$
BEGIN
  PERFORM private.notify_attendance_changed(NEW.party_id, NEW.event_id);
  RETURN NULL;
END;
$function$

door_wrapper__reading: The fourth wrapper is read separately and correctly has NO old-pair branch: one helper call, no IS DISTINCT FROM. public.door_scan_events is append-only by construction (it carries no write policy at all), so there is no update whose old night could differ from its new one. Counting it among the three would have hidden a real regression in one of them.
realtime_config__reading: suspend is still false, read at the timestamp above. This one is recorded for the day of the first night rather than for today: a suspend: true at 22:00 makes the whole phase a no-op with no error anywhere. private_only is still not returned by this endpoint, so its state is still unproved here and still needs a behavioural check.

what_these_probes_cannot_settle: THE MANAGEMENT API BYPASSES RLS. Every probe above ran as supabase_read_only_user through /database/query, so not one of them proves that a real member session is refused. LIVE-06 is NOT closed by this file. The policy exists, it is a SELECT policy, its rendered predicate asks the door question — and that is a statement about the catalogue, not about an authenticated browser. What closes LIVE-06 is procedure P7 in plan 38-07, and nothing before it. LIVE-01 likewise: the triggers exist, but no message has been observed arriving at a subscribed client, which is P1 and P2.
